description: Từ đợt re-review (claude:fable): (M) charset.test.ts:91, ngưỡng thời gian 1500 ms vẫn pass với code cũ, nên bỏ hoặc so với baseline TextEncoder; (L) media-sniff.ts:220, text UTF-16 có U+FFFD bị nhận nhầm là audio/mpeg, sửa bằng TextDecoder fatal; (L) uuencode.ts:106, cảnh báo thiếu ký tự báo nhầm, sửa lại lời cảnh báo; (L) Base64Charset.tsx:52, đưa bytesToBase64 và đếm code point vào useMemo; (L) Base64Media.tsx:247, BlobFrame cố định 'application/pdf'. Lead đề xuất thêm: gộp sniffMime của encoding.ts với media-sniff; bọc try/catch cho từng module trong browser-check; giới hạn kích thước hoặc lấy mẫu khi detectCharset chạy trên input lớn; nhận dạng UTF-16 không BOM cho văn bản CJK.

handoff.summary:
t-34ae.2 is done. All 9 items are implemented across 5 local commits on the current branch (175bdb6..a89fa6e), not pushed. Lead wrote everything directly as the single writer; no peer wrote code.

Commits:
- 6c32772: items 2, 3, 6
- 38eae9d: items 1, 8, 9
- 772c8de: items 4, 5, 7
- b40a6a1: fix for the reviewer's fail on item 9
- a89fa6e: tests and docstring for the re-review findings

Per item:
1. DONE. charset.test.ts: the 1500 ms bound is replaced by a deterministic count of `TextEncoder.prototype.encode` calls, with the spy restored in `finally`. Against the old code it fails with 1,050,000 calls, against the new code it passes with 1.
2. DONE. media-sniff.ts `isUtf16Text` uses `TextDecoder` with `fatal` and `stream:true`, so a genuine U+FFFD stays text and a lone surrogate is not text. Tests in media-sniff.test.ts cover the old audio/mpeg case `'Hi � there'` and a surrogate pair cut at the 4 KB boundary.
3. DONE. uuencode.ts warns only when characters that carry data bits are missing (`ceil(count*4/3)`), not when stripped padding is missing. The new message names both causes: stripped trailing spaces or truncation. Tests are in uuencode.test.ts.
4. DONE. Base64Charset.tsx: the Base64 output and the code-point count are in `useMemo`.
5. DONE, with an interpretation note. The task record's Vietnamese text, "BlobFrame cố định 'application/pdf'", means pin it to application/pdf. The brief's English said the opposite ("is hardcoded → use detected"). The code already passed the detected type, so BlobFrame now always uses a `PDF_MIME` constant as defense-in-depth for the unsandboxed iframe. It is reached only for kind 'pdf', so behavior is the same.
6. DONE. `encoding.sniffMime` and `extensionForMime` are removed. Base64File uses media-sniff's `sniffMimeType`/`extensionFor`/`mediaType`. Two visible changes: the image preview is gated on `mediaType().preview==='image'`, so HEIC/TIFF no longer show a broken preview, and default filenames follow the richer detected type (.txt/.json/.html instead of .bin).
7. DONE. browser-check.mjs runs each check module in its own try/catch, reports errors via `fail()`, and the remaining modules still run.
8. DONE. charset.ts `detectCharset`: the heuristics read a 64 KB prefix (`DETECT_SAMPLE_BYTES`), with the legacy scoring using `stream:true`. The BOM, ASCII-only and strict UTF-8 checks and the parity check still use the whole input. A low-confidence result notes when it came from a sample.
9. DONE (conservative). `guessUtf16Cjk` fires only when all of these hold:
   - the input has a C0 byte other than tab/LF/CR;
   - every code unit is CJK or printable ASCII;
   - at least 2 anchor units (ASCII, U+3000-301F or U+FFxx);
   - at least 4 CJK units, making up at least 30%;
   - exactly one byte order fits.
   It is never run on all-ASCII input. It misses short text and text with fewer than two punctuation/space/ASCII units.

Review history:
- First review (claude:opus): FAIL on item 9. ASCII + form feed was detected as UTF-16BE, and legacy CJK + a stray control byte as UTF-16. Fixed in b40a6a1.
- Re-review (claude:opus): PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. No regression against base in 1.4M fuzzed realistic documents or the earlier probes. Its findings (1 medium test-coverage, 2 low docstring) were fixed in a89fa6e.

Model switch: I tried codex:gpt-6-astra for the reviewer first, but Codex is paused on its usage limit until 2026-10-10T05:35Z, so both reviews ran on claude:opus.
candidate: 6c32772 fix(base64): single MIME sniffer, UTF-16 U+FFFD text, uuencode short-line warning — src/lib/media-sniff.ts, src/lib/media-sniff.test.ts, src/lib/uuencode.ts, src/lib/uuencode.test.ts, src/lib/encoding.ts, src/lib/encoding.test.ts, src/tools/base64/Base64File.tsx (items 2,3,6)
38eae9d fix(charset): sample large inputs, detect BOM-less UTF-16 CJK, deterministic perf test — src/lib/charset.ts, src/lib/charset.test.ts (items 1,8,9)

772c8de refactor(base64): memoize charset output, pin PDF frame type, isolate browser checks — src/tools/base64/Base64Charset.tsx, src/tools/base64/Base64Media.tsx, scripts/browser-check.mjs (items 4,5,7)

b40a6a1 fix(charset): keep stray control bytes from tipping text into UTF-16 CJK — src/lib/charset.ts, src/lib/charset.test.ts, src/lib/media-sniff.test.ts, src/lib/encoding.test.ts (fix for the reviewer's fail on item 9 + low findings)
a89fa6e test(charset): cover the GBK/EUC-KR control-byte cases; document residual risk — src/lib/charset.ts, src/lib/charset.test.ts (re-review findings)
scope: Not touched: nav/layout, CI, package.json/deps, other tools, .alp/tasks (t-34ae.1.json modified and t-34ae.2.json untracked are main's, left uncommitted)
verification: Final run at HEAD a89fa6e: `pnpm check` (typecheck && lint && test && build && smoke) exit 0. Test Files 15 passed (15); Tests 315 passed (315); vite ✓ built in 308ms; smoke: OK (35 tool routes)
Final run at a89fa6e: `pnpm browser` exit 0. browser-check: OK (35 tool routes + home + 404, 0 console/CSP errors)
Same check + browser also passed at 772c8de and b40a6a1

Tests checked against old code: item 1 spy test fails on dc82dc7^ ('expected encode to be called 1 times, but got 1050000'); item 2 media-sniff test fails on the pre-change media-sniff.ts; the control-byte tests fail on 772c8de (utf-16be) and pass at HEAD
Reviewer 1 (claude:opus, alp-child-03bcee92...): FAIL. Criteria 1-8 pass, 9 fails (ASCII/legacy + control byte detected as UTF-16) → fixed in b40a6a1

Reviewer 2 (claude:opus, alp-child-33a5ebf1...): PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. 0 changes vs base in 10,255/56,376/576 probe variants, 1.1M fuzzed docs and 300k TSV/CSV docs; 302/302 src/lib tests. Findings: medium (GBK/EUC-KR tests did not cover the failing inputs) and 2 low docstring → all fixed in a89fa6e. No further review after a89fa6e (tests + comments only)
risks: Item 9 still has a synthetic-only false positive. Legacy text plus a stray control byte, plus two '0'-next-to-tab/LF anchors at the right offsets with no CRLF, is still detected as BOM-less UTF-16LE: 222 of 26,136 reviewer-constructed inputs, 0 of 1.4M realistic ones. The guess is low confidence and the user can override it. This is documented in the docstring.

Item 9 recall: single-sentence UTF-16 CJK text with only one punctuation mark and no spaces, and pure ideographs, are not detected (by design, conservative). Base never detected BOM-less CJK, so this is not a regression.

Item 3: lines whose trailing zero-valued data characters were stripped (e.g. an 'M' line ending in zero bytes) now get a neutral warning where the old code said nothing; the message says it may be stripped spaces.
Item 6: Base64File's default download names and image-preview gating changed (more specific extensions; HEIC/TIFF/PSD no longer shown as a broken ). Not covered by screenshots.
a89fa6e (tests + docstring only) was not independently re-reviewed after the re-review; the full check and browser check pass on it.
Item 5 follows the Vietnamese task text (pin application/pdf), not the brief's English (use the detected type); behavior is identical because only PDFs reach BlobFrame.
discovered: Base64File has no browser-check coverage of the new MIME behavior (filename extension for text/json/html and the preview gate); consider adding it to scripts/checks/base64-*.mjs.

Base64Charset's code-point count still spreads the whole decoded string into an array (useMemo now, but O(n) memory); a counting loop like charset.ts codePointCount could be exported and reused if large inputs matter.
Possible follow-up for item 9 recall: an opt-in 'UTF-16 (no BOM)' hint in the Base64Charset UI, instead of loosening the heuristic, for single-sentence CJK text.
